extracted.intended_audience: members of the media and journalists covering health/medical topics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for reporters, editors, producers, and other media representatives on permitted access to, use of, and restrictions governing JAMA Network prepublication (embargoed) materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo prohibition on public disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: JAMA Network grants prepublication access to articles to selected members of the media who agree not to publish, broadcast, post online, or otherwise place information about embargoed content in the public domain until the time of their publication by the JAMA Network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not release any information from embargoed content before the embargo lifts (the time/day the article is published online).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted activities during embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: During this embargo period individuals granted access to articles may read them, discuss their findings with the authors, and consult with other experts for the purpose of drafting reports, news stories, or other coverage for release at the time of article publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use embargoed materials only to prepare coverage for release when the embargo lifts; discussion and expert consultation are allowed for preparation but not for public dissemination prior to lift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of embargoed materials
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the PDF of the full article scheduled for publication, the JAMA Network can provide images from an article. All of this material is subject to the embargo and is furnished exclusively for use in coverage of JAMA Network articles, and for no other purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any images or full-text PDFs provided under embargo are covered by the same non-disclosure restriction and may not be repurposed for other uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access equals agreement to restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: By requesting access to JAMA Network embargoed materials, members of the media agree to adhere to the above restrictions and also to the following specific policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesting access functions as assent to the embargo policy and related rules; contact Media Relations for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo timing rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoes vary and lift the time and day articles are published online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the exact publication time/day for each article; embargo lift is tied to online publication timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible recipients for embargoed access
rubrics_metrics.description: JAMA Network will grant credentials to its embargoed content to: Reporters, writers, editors, and producers with staff credentials from newspapers, magazines, online news services, wire services, radio or television networks and stations; Independent journalists (including bloggers) and editors who regularly cover health-related topics (Note: Individuals will be required to provide examples of recent work); Representatives of some academic, government, or hospital media/public relations departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent journalists must provide examples of recent work demonstrating regular coverage of health topics; institutional PR representatives may be eligible in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible recipients (who will not be granted access)
rubrics_metrics.description: JAMA Network will not grant access to its embargoed content to: Public relations firms, advertising agencies, or production companies with no immediate affiliation to the authors or a specific article; Writers/editors or other contributors for patient publications created and distributed by industry, such as pharmaceutical companies or device manufacturers; Representatives of industry including pharmaceutical companies or device manufacturers; Financial or industry analysts; Publications or websites supported by industry, including patient advocacy groups; Representatives of corporate media/public relations, advertising, or marketing departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry-affiliated individuals and organizations, financial analysts, and industry-supported publications are explicitly excluded from embargo access to avoid conflicts of interest and commercial misuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for breaking embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: JAMA Network reviews embargo breaks on a case-by-case basis. Circumstances of the embargo violation will be evaluated before a determination is made regarding appropriate penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalties may include but are not limited to loss of access to embargoed materials, loss of media credentials to JAMA Network events, and suspension of the media outlet from receiving embargoed materials. If suspended, the reporter and media outlet are responsible for reapplying after the suspension period ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for maintaining embargo system
rubrics_metrics.description: Rationale summarized by the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors: 'Doctors in practice need to have research reports available in full detail before they can advise patients about the reports’ conclusions…. For the media, the embargo creates a ‘level playing field,' which most reporters and writers appreciate since it minimizes the pressure on them to publish stories before competitors when they have not had time to prepare carefully.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embargoes are intended to provide time for accurate reporting, protect clinical decision-making, and minimize market/economic disruption from premature release.
